title: XRP Reclaims $1.10 As Traders Watch Breakout Momentum
summary: XRP Reclaims $1.10 As Traders Watch Breakout Momentum - Read the full analysis.
content:
XRP has pushed back above the key $1.10 psychological threshold, signaling renewed bullish momentum following days of range-bound consolidation.
The price recovery is being supported by a steady pick-up in derivatives volume and renewed net inflows into US spot XRP ETFs.
On-chain data highlights a growing concentration of trading activity during major financial market hours, pointing to increased professional participation.
Traders are now focused on immediate overhead resistance between $1.12 and $1.15, where key moving averages present the next hurdle for buyers.
A sustained close above this resistance cluster could validate the breakout, while failing to defend $1.10 risks a retreat back toward $1.00 support.
For now, short-term momentum favors the bulls as market participants gauge whether spot demand can absorb ongoing profit-taking.

title: Wyoming Stable Token Commission Moves FRNT Infrastructure To Chainlink CCIP
summary: Wyoming Stable Token Commission Moves FRNT Infrastructure To Chainlink CCIP - Read the full analysis.
content:
The Wyoming Stable Token Commission has migrated its sovereign Frontier Stable Token (FRNT) to Chainlink’s Cross-Chain Interoperability Protocol (CCIP).
The state entity fully deprecated its previous integration with LayerZero following a security review that raised operational and disclosure concerns.
As the first public-entity stablecoin in the U.S., FRNT leverages CCIP to maintain secure cross-chain functionality across eight major blockchain networks.

Commission leadership stated that CCIP was the only infrastructure capable of satisfying Wyoming's strict security and institutional compliance standards.

The multi-year partnership secures state-backed digital asset transfers while preserving reserve yield generated for Wyoming’s public education fund.

title: Avalanche: Why AVAX’s rally faces THIS test after $2.4M whale deposit
summary: AVAX approaches $7 as surging volume and bullish positioning confront fresh whale-led exchange supply.
content:
Avalanche (AVAX) is at a critical technical crossroads as a $2.4 million AVAX deposit onto exchanges threatens to stall its recent price recovery.
On-chain tracking data shows the substantial transfer from a high-net-worth address directly into exchange wallets, a move that typically signals imminent profit-taking.
This sudden surge in exchange liquidity puts immediate pressure on bulls, who must absorb the potential sell-side volume to prevent an overhead rejection.
Despite solid network fundamentals—supported by rising real-world asset tokenization and steady staking lockups—short-term momentum now faces heightened downside risk.
Technical indicators show that if buyers fail to hold primary support levels against this whale distribution, AVAX could lose its breakout momentum and retreat back into lower consolidation zones.
Traders are closely monitoring spot order books to determine if broader market demand can absorb the influx without triggering a deeper market pull-back.

title: Ship crossings in Strait of Hormuz drop amid US-Iran tensions: Reuters
summary:
The reduced ship crossings highlight escalating geopolitical tensions, potentially disrupting global trade and impacting energy markets.
The post Ship crossings in Strait of Hormuz drop amid US-Iran tensions: Reuters appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content:
Commercial shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has plunged to single-digit daily transits amid escalating US-Iran tensions.
Vessel tracking data from Kpler shows confirmed transits dropped by roughly 95% compared to pre-conflict averages.
Heightened security hazards, soaring insurance costs, and recent tanker attacks have forced fleet operators to halt transit operations.
Iranian maritime authorities are enforcing strict coastal transit demands while US naval forces maintain blockade and escort operations.
With the strategic corridor carrying a fifth of global crude oil and LNG, persistent disruptions continue driving risk premiums across energy markets

title: Hawkish RBI minutes spark volatility in India’s bond market
summary:
RBI's hawkish stance may trigger higher borrowing costs, impacting global markets by strengthening the US dollar and pressuring gold prices.
The post Hawkish RBI minutes spark volatility in India’s bond market appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content:
Indian government bond yields spiked after hawkish Reserve Bank of India (RBI) minutes revealed MPC members are prepared to raise interest rates if inflation pressures broaden.


Benchmark 10-year yields surged to a two-month high of 6.87% as heavy selling pressure swept sovereign debt markets.
Policymakers cited persistent food and fuel price volatility alongside rising raw material costs as key catalysts for potential monetary tightening.
The sell-off was further exacerbated by rising global crude oil prices, prompting swap markets to quickly price in rate hike risks for late 2026.
The unexpected shift in central bank tone has shattered expectations for an extended pause, triggering heightened volatility across domestic fixed-income assets.

title: Asian currencies rise as US bond buyback plan faces skepticism: WSJ
summary:
Investor skepticism over U.S. bond buybacks may shift interest rate expectations, impacting global currency dynamics and gold market trends.
The post Asian currencies rise as US bond buyback plan faces skepticism: WSJ appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content:
Asian currencies gained ground against the U.S. dollar as global markets grew skeptical of Washington’s expanded debt-buyback plan.

The U.S. Treasury Department moved to double its weekly bond repurchases in an attempt to cap surging long-term borrowing costs.
However, an initial drop in Treasury yields quickly reversed as bond investors concluded buybacks offer only temporary liquidity rather than deficit reduction.

The fading impact of the Treasury intervention pulled the U.S. Dollar Index lower, opening space for regional currencies to bounce back.
Analysts warn that unless structural fiscal concerns are resolved, persistent weakness in the greenback will keep Asian exchange rates elevated.

title: Brazil invests $444M to enhance AI ecosystem and supercomputing
summary:
Brazil's AI investment aims to boost technological sovereignty, reduce reliance on foreign tech, and position itself as a global AI leader.
The post Brazil invests $444M to enhance AI ecosystem and supercomputing appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content:
Brazil’s government has committed 2.3 billion reais ($444 million) from its national science fund to accelerate domestic AI and supercomputing capabilities.
The plan allocates $251 million toward a Rio de Janeiro facility partnering with Chinese firms Huawei and iFlytek to train localized language models.
An additional $193 million is earmarked for an AI supercomputing cluster in Rio Grande do Norte designed to rank among the world's top ten.

President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva framed the investment as a strategic push toward data sovereignty and domestic infrastructure autonomy.

By balancing procurement between American hardware providers and Chinese tech firms, Brazil aims to build computing power without relying on a single foreign superpower.

title: Oil set for second weekly rise amid US-Iran tensions affecting supply
summary:
Geopolitical tensions may sustain elevated oil prices, impacting global economic stability and influencing energy policy decisions worldwide.
The post Oil set for second weekly rise amid US-Iran tensions affecting supply appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content:
Crude oil prices are on track for a second consecutive weekly gain, with Brent hovering near $94 and WTI topping $86 a barrel amid escalating US-Iran hostilities.
The price rally is being driven by severe supply disruption fears as the ongoing conflict significantly restricts commercial transit through the Strait of Hormuz.
Market momentum accelerated after Washington outlined plans for an "economic D-day" aimed at completely isolating Iran's international financial and commercial channels.
Further tightening regional supply risks, the United Arab Emirates recently suspended all economic and financial transactions with Tehran.
Analysts warn that unless transit security is restored in the Middle East, the embedded geopolitical risk premium could soon push Brent crude well past the $100 per barrel threshold.

title: TerraPay and TPBank Link Up for Real-Time Cross-Border Payments
summary:
Vietnam's TPBank will use TerraPay's 156-country network to offer real-time outbound international payments without building bilateral banking relationships.
The post TerraPay and TPBank Link Up for Real-Time Cross-Border Payments appeared first on The Fintech Times.
content:
Global infrastructure provider TerraPay has partnered with Vietnam’s TPBank to enable real-time cross-border transfers across more than 150 countries.
Through a single API integration, TPBank connects directly to TerraPay’s network, avoiding the complexity of negotiating individual correspondent banking relationships.
The collaboration supports two-way, direct account-to-account and account-to-wallet transactions, eliminating traditional intermediary bank delays.

All international transactions under the agreement remain fully compliant with the State Bank of Vietnam’s foreign exchange and anti-money laundering regulations.
The expansion targets Vietnam's surging digital payment market, connecting local customers to major remittance corridors across Asia, Europe, and the Americas.

title: Ross Posts 13% Sales Jump as Inflation Drives Shoppers to Off-Price Retailers
summary:
Off-price retailer Ross Stores saw “robust” sales growth in the quarter ended Aug. 1 as both existing customers and new ones sought prices lower than those of mainstream retailers, CEO Jim Conroy said during a Thursday (Aug. 20) earnings call. “We really want to be there for a customer that is battling higher gas prices […]
The post Ross Posts 13% Sales Jump as Inflation Drives Shoppers to Off-Price Retailers appeared first on PYMNTS.com.
content:
Off-price giant Ross Stores reported a 13% jump in second-quarter total sales to $6.3 billion as persistent inflation drives shoppers toward value chains.
Same-store sales surged 10% during the quarter, fueled primarily by an uptick in customer traffic across all income levels.
Elevated gas prices and general living expenses continue pushing consumers away from full-price department stores in search of deeper discounts.
Strong demand helped net earnings reach $851 million for the period, prompting management to raise its full-year profit outlook.
Executives confirmed the company will maintain its core pricing model to preserve its price advantage over mainstream retail competitors.
